expected_artifacts: eda_report.: pairable-user fractions, per-user count histograms, unknown-slot rates per group under prior_days, key-sparsity table, train-only aux-target correlation table, validation user/video overlap stats

Shortlist of 2-3 next-candidate parameter dicts mapped to run(context, parameters) -> CandidateOutput (e.g., history_features with user_author+recency+video_age, m=20, prior_days; group_softmax K=4 T=1.0; multi_task is_click aux_weight=0.3)
Edge-case notes (single-class users, duplicate negatives, first-day unknown rows) translated into synthetic fixtures for test_candidate.py same-user sampling/group tests
feature_hypotheses: Smoothed (user, author) long_view rate (prior_days, m around 20) is the highest-value history group because it varies within a user and crosses with video/author fields; test first via history_features with use_user_author enabled.

recency and video_age buckets add within-user temporal signal; enabling them alongside user_author should beat user_rate alone, since user-side-only groups contribute nothing through the first-order term under within-user GAUC.

is_click as a single auxiliary head at aux_weight 0.1-0.3 improves validation GAUC through shared embeddings given its ~0.76 train correlation with long_view; play_time (censoring bias) and is_like (1.9% prevalence) are deprioritized.

group_softmax with K=4 and temperature 1.0 approximates the evaluated within-user list better than single-pair BPR on users with at least 5 mixed-label impressions; duplicate negatives within groups reduce effective K and must be deduplicated at sampling time.
leakage_risks: Fitting quantile buckets, smoothed-rate tables, or global priors on validation rows - all statistics must be computed on train rows only
leave_one_out lets train rows see later same-user days; EDA conclusions must be drawn under prior_days, using leave_one_out only to measure the gap
Unsmoothed per-key rates memorize labels at low counts (a key seen once with one positive gets rate 1.0); smoothing m must stay well above zero

Repeatedly tuning feature subsets or smoothing against validation GAUC turns validation into a training signal; EDA selects candidates from train distributions and validation is consumed once via the official evaluator
Using validation/test dates or any future information in recency/video_age; unknown keys must map to the reserved slot, not the prior bucket
Requesting or inferring hidden-test statistics, or aggregating any statistic across splits
data.objective: Plan one compact, train/validation-only EDA pass that quantifies within-user label structure, history-feature coverage under the prior_days scheme, and auxiliary-target signal, so the next registered candidate (bpr, group_softmax, history_features, multi_task) is configured from evidence while respecting the trusted run(context, parameters) -> CandidateOutput contract and the official evaluator.
questions: What fraction of train and validation users have both long_view positives and negatives, and what are the per-user impression and positive-count distributions (pairability for BPR/group_softmax, expected skipped users)?
Under prior_days, what share of train rows falls in each feature group's unknown/reserved slot, and how do key-count distributions justify smoothing m in {5, 20, 100}?
How sparse are (user, author), (user, tab), and (tab, duration-bucket) keys - what share have fewer than 5 train observations where the smoothed prior dominates?
On train rows only, how strongly do is_click, is_like, and log1p-scaled play_time correlate with long_view overall and within low-count user/video strata (multi_task head priority)?
What share of validation users and videos appear in train, and how heterogeneous are within-user validation labels (do user-side-only groups act only through crosses)?
At K in {4, 8}, how many duplicate negative rows appear within same-user groups, and what is the within-user spread of baseline FM scores (temperature sanity check for group_softmax)?
required_inputs: DATA CARD: field definitions (user, video, author, tab, dur_bucket), long_view label definition, official train/validation split protocol
Train arrays: train_x, train_y, train_users plus row timestamps/dates needed for recency and video_age buckets
Validation arrays: valid_x, valid_users (metrics obtained only via context.evaluate_validation; no evaluator reimplementation)
